answer: I would anchor trust in Content-hash chain linking answers across epochs. With each answer hashed into the previous epoch's chain, a single ferrous check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that each answer hashed into the previous epoch's chain — so privacy survives, and the mirror is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the cipher of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
